land.text: 'a thin strip of land' between the Sarayu river and the Himalayan hills, east of the Rohini, which 'was the western border of the Koliyas'; Ramagrama (Ramgram Municipality, Parasi District, Nepal) 'a major city of the Koliya kingdom' and Devadaha; the page gives no boundary, so a 35 km disc stands for the republic

successors.note: Infobox 'Conquered by Vidudabha of Kosala: c. 5th century BCE'; the page adds that 'Ajatasattu of Magadha may have conquered the Koliyas directly', so Magadha (magadha-haryanka-dynasty) is the alternative heir.

capitals.name: Ramagrama (Ramgram)

ledger.note: c. 7th century BCE: the Koliya republic is established east of the Rohini. Infobox 'Established: c. 7th century BCE', 'Aristocratic Republic', 'Capital: Ramagama'; the text has 'By the sixth century BCE, the Koliyas, the Sakyas...'. -650 is the middle of the page's century, so the year is bridging.

ledger.note: c. 5th century BCE: Vidudabha of Kosala annexes the Koliyas. Infobox 'Conquered by Vidudabha of Kosala: c. 5th century BCE'; 'Shortly after the Buddha's death, the Kausalya king' invaded; 'The Koliyas likewise disappeared as a polity and as a tribe soon after their annexation'. -460 is bridging, set before Kosala's own end in -451.

certainty.note: A tribal republic known from Buddhist texts; no boundary is given and the dates are centuries.

sources.title: Koliya
sources.note: Infobox (Ramagama, aristocratic republic, established c. 7th century BCE, conquered by Vidudabha c. 5th century BCE), the Rohini as western border, the Sarayu, the feud with the Shakyas, Magadha as alternative conqueror.

sources.title: Ramagrama
sources.note: Location of the Koliya city (Ramgram Municipality, Parasi District, Nepal); no coordinates; no dated Koliya sentences.

notes: Dates are bridging (see shakya): the page gives only centuries, so both events are confidence 1. The page contradicts itself on the capital (infobox Ramagama, body Devadaha). The Rohini river 'was the western border of the Koliyas' and the Anoma or Rapti river 'separated the Koliyas from the kingdom of Kosala' in the south-west; the disc is centred on Ramagrama, not on a computed strip. Gazetteer: Ramagrama and Devadaha are not places; a coordinate disc stands in.
